title: Count Complete Tree Nodes
statement:
Given the root of a complete binary tree, return the number of the nodes in the tree.

Design an algorithm that runs in less than O(n) time complexity by leveraging the fact that it is a complete tree (all levels are completely filled except possibly the last level, which is filled from left to right).
inputFormat: A single line containing space-separated strings mapping the level-order traversal of the tree (`null` for missing nodes).
outputFormat: A single integer denoting the node count.
constraints:
0 <= The number of nodes in the tree <= 5 * 10^4
-10^4 <= Node.val <= 10^4

starterCode.python:
import sys
line = sys.stdin.read().split()
if not line:
    print(0)
else:
    # While the total length could just be calculated by the nodes given, try executing left/right depths checks for practice on O(log^2 N).
    print(len([x for x in line if x != 'null']))
